questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: When choosing the destination it was crucial for me to find a university with high academic character and a culture somewhat similar to Danish.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: There were definitely pros and cons during the stay. I think that even though thought I would fit in culture-wise, I found out that the people were a bit different than expected. The academic level was high, as expected, which I was very pleased with.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was easy, emails, calls and the information desk were super helpful.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I received emails and also contacted the information desk.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: Very difficult! I was victim of scam and ended up not having anywhere to live for a week, therefore was desperate to find an apartment. The one I ended up living in was super expensive compared to my co-workers. There were no helpful solutions from the host university.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Be super aware of scam! There are so many people trying to take advantage of the student's situation since everyone knows that housing is a big issue.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Definitely needed guidance for finding housing. I personally contacted every agency in the city after the scam, to be sure not to be fooled again. They have a concept of 4+4 meaning that they rent the apartment 4+4 years. So when I needed a place for 10 months, nobody wanted to rent anything to me.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: All kinds of sports, cultural experiences and trips. The Erasmus is very prominent in Bologna and a lot of opportunities are available.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I did not attend any activities, however, I think the activities were good and fun for everyone.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer:
I in general went on a lot of trips around Italy and experienced a lot of cities. 
Among others Road trip in Tuscany, Cinque Terre, Napoli and the Beach in Rimini. Use the Flixbus, often a very easy and cheap solution.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: I think it was ok, everyone is late in Italy without that being an issue. They are openminded however do prefer to speak Italian, so that was definitely a difficulty sometimes. At the university there is also a more strict hierarchy, you are not friends with the professor in the same way as you sometimes can be "friends" with your supervisor/professor in Denmark,

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Find some people from the universities as they often know english. I also found a very good friend in my gym. There were only gym classes which made it easier to make friends during the training.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Definitely the language, and the fact that people would rather speak Italian rather than English. That left me feeling a bit lonely sometimes.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Drinks, snacks and talks after work. Everyone goes for a cheap Aperol one or two times a week after work, a very fun and social way of ending your workday.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1) Learn a bit of Italian before arriving and 2) get help for finding housing!
3) I had a very good Danish supervisor to give me support regarding the demands of the University of Copenhagen, I found that very helpful and calming for my stay.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: I went to Bologna for a weekend, three months before starting my stay to see the city and just have a feeling for where to look for housing and things like this. And also for meeting the people of my laboratory.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Trying to live abroad and trying to live with friends.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Coping and navigating in the fact that the co-workers do not always speak English even though you are around. During lunchtime, this was particularly tough. So the greatest challenge during the stay was to accept and understand that there is nothing wrong with me when they don't speak English, they were just not as interested as I expected in my points of view.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
